diagnosis: The harness never reached a comparison: it timed out because the case module is too slow. The document's subject is not in question — the failure is in the case set's construction (an exact-arithmetic Decimal sweep over hundreds of values per type, a Taylor series summed to 80 digits per element, and a fresh ONNX Runtime model built per batch). The document leaves accuracy to the profile's guidelines, so the heavy exact-arithmetic reference is not required to decide any case; the special values, sign, shape and type are the required checks and they are cheap.
instruction: Reduce the case module so the harness finishes within its budget, without weakening the required checks. Concretely: (1) in `sweep_correctness` and `sweep_domain`, cut the random samples from 200+200 and 300 per type to at most 20 per type, and keep the boundary/subnormal values; (2) replace the per-element Decimal Taylor series with a cheaper reference — compute `np.arctan` in float64 and round to the type, or precompute the reference once per distinct operand and cache it — since the document leaves accuracy to the profile's guidelines and the departure is reported, not required; (3) build the ONNX Runtime session once per dtype (or once total) and reuse it across the sweeps instead of constructing a model per call; (4) keep `sweep_special_values` and `sweep_sign_and_shape` as they are, since they are the required exact checks and are cheap. Re-run and report the sweeps' summaries and any failures.
